attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post, describing the Annenberg poll.

semantics.note: A firm present-tense observation that data-center opposition crosses party lines. The poll he cites supplies the 'local construction' framing.

contract.note: Reading 'crosses party lines' as substantial opposition in both parties is the ordinary, fair reading. Using the poll's fieldwork period as the target period is reasonable.

evidence.note: Annenberg release reproduced by Phys.org, available 2026-08-11. It reports majorities of Democrats (69%), Republicans (54%) and independents (53%) opposing new local data centers, for June 16–July 19, 2026.

reviews.rationale: The poll Marcus cites shows majority opposition to new local data centers among Democrats, Republicans and independents. That meets the support condition. Opposition is higher among Democrats, but Republican opposition is a majority, not marginal. The release's caution about subgroup uncertainty doesn't undo a 54% majority.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence summarising the Annenberg poll in his post.

semantics.note: A firm observation that opposition is rising fast, with the poll kept as the stated source. Nothing added or dropped.

contract.note: Reading 'rising fast' as a substantial rise over a short interval, beyond sampling uncertainty, is fair and ordinary. The two-wave comparison matches the poll he references.

evidence.note: Annenberg's original topline: opposition rose from 48.9% (Feb–Mar) to 60.6% (Jun–Jul), +11.8 points, 95% CI +6.9 to +16.6. The same-respondent check gives +12.5. Available 2026-08-11.

reviews.rationale: Over about four months, comparable survey waves show local data-center opposition up nearly 12 points. The confidence interval excludes zero on both the wave-to-wave and the same-respondent measure. Under the plain reading, a substantial, significant rise over a short interval counts as rising fast.
